2A-b patch notes:
SpoilerPopulation & Infrastructure no longer grants any income. Instead it has upkeep equal to vanilla farming
Tech-Mining now brings in an income equal to the vanilla income of Population & Infrastructure. Which is a flat sum of 10k. It no longer has an upkeep. Considering the increase of upkeep for all the colony infrastructure. Tech-Mining will now be the simplest industry to profit from short-termly

Support Doctrine no longer gives Ordnance Expertise
This has been removed in further attempt to make Support Doctrine not just a straight up upgrade to your entire fleet. While it only affects ships without officers, it still feels too impactful for how little micromanagement is actually being done. Whereas Neural Link, Derelict Operations, Cybernetic Augmentation require new ways of building your character due to having 3 less skill points. Support Doctrine remained unchanged. And because of how effective it was, it felt like a mandatory pick that trivialised the entire experience by making your fleets just straight up better with 0 economical investment. Contrary to spamming mercenary officers or spending fat dollars on repairing broken s-modded ships.
The game doesn't have enough ultra difficult combat encounters due to Remnants being significantly nerfed and crisis being more rare. So Support Doctrine did not serve the purpose of making the gameplay better, but only worse due to how powerful it was

To compensate for Support Doctrine and Best of the Best nerfs. These admiral skills can now be acquired only after 3 skill points being spent in Leadership tree instead of 4. Making it simpler for them to be picked up when running character builds that do not center around early Leadership skills

Blueprint price multipliers have been reduced from 10 to 5. This was done because being able to sell a Paragon blueprint for 7 million credits felt out of place, considering Tri-Tachyon only pays a singular million for the Ziggurat

Intelligence Cores and Survey Data now has twice as high value
This has been done to encourage players to give up their Alpha Cores to factions in the Core Worlds instead of keeping them around to be later bullied to death by Hegemony

Removed weapon losing mechanic from the mod
This feature is incompatible with other mod experiences and Omega weapons.
The additional 50% weapon found and 400% more wings found. And finding more hullmods has remained however. Which means you will have 50% more Omega weapons from killing Omegas in your playthrough

Made officers level up only 4 times as fast instead of 8
This has been done because it felt like it made Mentoring pointless. It also made it very difficult to naturally build your officers with them rapidly going from level 1 to 5 in the span of 2 combat engagements. Now it'll take 3 combat engagements. So, don't worry... Their leveling is still going to be really fast

Increased the amount of ships and weapons being produced from an industry point by a factor of 4. This has been done because colonies are no longer as profitable as they used to be. The player will no longer be able to establish seven high industry colonies in the span of 2 years in the late game. Because it's no longer going to be that profitable. And growing of colonies is also slower. Therefore the amount of ships you can produce from a heavy industry for yourself is now incredibly high as long as you have the money to back that up. It however isn't high enough to make the administrator skill negligible

Removed the extreme cost of hazard pay. Hazard pay is now the same as in vanilla if it comes to paying for immigration points. However it now brings up the migration to 40 instead of 5. Making launching colonies far easier. The increased amount of points needed to raise a colony from higher levels. As these numbers now scale 3 times as strongly as they did in vanilla. Means that bringing a colony from level 5 to 6 on a planet with horrible high hazard rating is going to be expensive and time-consuming. However bringing it from 3 to 4 should be practical trivial for all intends and purposes

Picking Elite Skills for officers and Fully Integrating AI Cores now gives 50% of bonus experience instead of 0%.
Initial bonus XP from building-in s-mods has been increased for all ships by 25%
These changes are meant to make fleets more flexible. And also make the player feel less guilty about selling an s-modded ship instead of scavenging. They're also meant to help players that use Best of the Best to get all the necessary s-mods for their ships in a short period of time

Greatly increased base salvaging rewards. Does not affect salvaging campaign objects.
The existence of scavenger in the game would imply that scavenging is actually a profitable craft. When in actuality, it's a waste of time. Pressing 6 after completing a battle will usually barely yield anything. And the amount of credits acquired from corpses is symbolic at best.
This change will now cause players to be able to recover large amounts of supplies, machinery and credits from killing enemies, Encouraging cannibalism of their fellow men. This also means that the post-battle salvage skill known as Salvaging is significantly more valuable

ECCM package now costs as much as Phase Anchor and can no longer be built-in. All variants that use ECCM package in the game have been adjusted to compensate for this change. Odyssey no longer has 10 additional OP as it had ECCM built-in by default
ECCM paired with incredible missile changes like Hurricane having 15 projectiles. Or Squall dealing 200 energy damage on top of the 150 kinetic damage package made it incredibly oppressive. Building it in into a ship like Gryphon felt mandatory because of how much value it granted. And now it felt even more ridiculous. ECCM package basically disables any meaningful anti-missile counterplay. So it is now treated like a premium hullmod that should be equipped only on specialist ships at a high price so it doesn't become mandatory

Safety Overrides now cost as much Phase Anchor instead of more. Additionally Safety Overrides has been buffed from their initial modded state. The range cut now occurs at 800 range instead of 600. And the peak operating time multiplier is 50% instead of 33%
This has been done because Safety Override ships find it much more difficult to survive in this modded version of Starsector. Energy weapons deal a lot more damage on average, no longer relying on long-term kiting. Ballistics have longer range making it simpler to focus damage on incoming SO ships.
Additionally in this mod SO has been nerfed by removing its attribute of increased manoeuvrability and base max movement speed. Now the SO only benefits from the 0-flux boost always being on. To compensate for this. The hullmod no longer costs as much. The player can now equip Unstable Injector to grant some of that old speed boost. And with more peak operating time and base range, NPC vessels can now operate more intelligently.
This does creates the fear of it being viable to make SO builds look exactly like normal builds. But I feel like with a huge base OP penalty, flux vents being more valuable. The player will be encouraged to equip short-ranged high flux spending high damage weapons that make use of mobility. Instead of relying on decreased in range artillery weapons. The exception to this might be frigates. But with increased flux venting... I don't know. We'll see

Ill-Advised modifications is now 10 times as less likely to occur as it was in vanilla. Instead of 5. This hullmod is no longer a d-mod. And instead a mandatory occurrence on Pather ships for example. Because of SO being now less valuable. The danger of this hullmod has been reduced to compensate

Derelict ships no longer have bonus movement speed. Their hull durability and armour has been increased to compensate with the exception of Rampart and Guardian. Guardian remains unchanged stat-wise. However Rampart's speed was reduced to vanilla standard as with all Derelicts.
With nerfed Remnants, Derelicts now looked too out of place. With high health pools they become bullet sponges of sorts that die very quickly anyway to powerful energy weapons and specialised anti-armour tools. They are now a cheap and disposable infantry that can be dealt with slowly through kiting just like in vanilla. Except more. This has been done as ridiculous Derelict speed made it very difficult to contest control points. Usually locking the player out from being able to deploy their fleet

Increased Nova's shield profile to 210 degrees.
Nova's suicidal behaviour paired with its shields now being of 0.8 value made it far too squishy for being 40 DP. To make up for this. Nova has now an even wider shield profile. Allowing it to commit into risky tactics without dying instantly to being moderately flanked

Reverted Invictus Lidar Array nerf.
Invictus Lidar Array cooldown was increased to 20 seconds due to the ship being able to snipe everything rapidly as long as it was not restricted by flux. This turned out to be stupid. As most capital ships at 50 DP can do that now. So it doesn't feel unique for being able to do so. Especially considering its incredible vulnerability to anti-armour damage like HIL

Replaced vanilla Fury variants with my own.
Replaced Falcon Attack variant with my own.
Fury and Falcon Attack variants felt really off in my opinion. They failed to provide any meaningful role on the battlefield. Note that the Ion Beam Falcon variant has not been changed. This affects the rare Falcon variant that uses 2 HMGs and 2 Pulse Laser, but is not equipped with ITU. I reworked it into a variant that has a Chaingun, HMG and 2 Pulse Lasers but has ITU instead of Heavy Armour.
Fury variants too have been completely reworked. Because I wanted them to be more challenging to fight without giving them any more nerfs. Basically. The beam Fury no longer exists. There's a Pulse Laser + Ion Cannon + Breach variant version now. The Fury Assault variant is somewhat identical. But it now equipped with IR Pulse Lasers in small slots instead of PD Lasers at the front

Removed Dragon targeting range penalty.
With the removal of ECCM from being an easily equippable hullmod and all the other missiles being extremely powerful. Dragon felt like it had the right to be as ridiculously strong, considering the fact that its actual anti-armour and anti-shield damage can be more easily neglected. And most PD weapons have enough range to shoot it down still. Especially after recent significant buffs to them

Doubled ammo capacity for Autopulse and Ion Pulser.
With various changes to energy weapons and Expanded Mags s-mod being heavily nerfed, Autopulse and Ion Pulser felt like they were late to the party. And equipped with no stamina. To compensate for this, they now have twice as much ammo. So fire away!

TPC has been nerfed. TPC now does 300 damage instead of 250 at 300 flux cost instead of 150 flux cost. Its range also has been reduced from 1k to 800 units. It now has twice as much maximum ammo. Allowing it do deal 24k energy damage in rapid succession as long as it has enough flux to do so. With increased flux venting however given to the Onslaught, as it now has 800 instead of 600. It usually does
TPC has been weirdly balanced in my opinion in vanilla. It was given to the Onslaught which at the same time has the flux stats similar to Dominator and Enforcer. Except while these two utilise weapons that are flux efficient and use missiles. Onslaught was given instead a unique energy weapon that is extremely difficult to fight against.
TPC served as a flux-free basically infinite range weapon that could be intensely spammed from long ranges. This made Hegemony fleets incredibly frustrating to fight against. Even when Onslaught had its 40 to 50 DP nerf.
To deal with this. The general damage dealt by TPC has been increased heavily. But at the same time this damage is no longer free. And Onslaught has to commit a large chunks of its flux pool and get in range to use it

Heavy Mortar now fires at double fire rate
Changed autofit tags for Heavy Mortar and Heavy Blaster to make Heavy Mortar a more common substitute for Chaingun than Heavy Blaster
Heavy Mortar although buffed with additional range still failed to pull the weight of being a specialist anti-armour tool. With a simpler solution being to rely on beam or energy weapons. With this balance change, the weapon will not necessarily be more effective. It will consume more flux for more damage. And the low hit strength will prevent it from becoming ridiculous. Faster enemies will dodge it. But yes, it will become far stronger. Worth its 7 OP cost, in spite of that not sounding like much.
Right now the issue is whether Heavy Mauler and Hypervelocity Driver are worth using in this mod. This will be closely analysed from now on

Removed LR tags from beam weapons. LR tags affect autofit and were causing weird interactions. The ships wouldn't choose to equip a Phase Lance as a substitute for Graviton Beam in spite of them having the same range now
Made Phase Lance no longer have an energy tag in autofit. This solves the issue of Heavy Blaster being often exchanged into Phase Lance by autofit. Now it will use Mining Blaster or Pulse Laser instead. Phase Lance will still replace various energy weapons however due to it having beam autofit tag
Made Mjolnir have a higher priority energy tag. This has been done mostly for Guardian

Guardian now has a hybrid slot at the front instead of ballistic as it was changed in this mod. And its base variant has been edited to prioritise Mjolnir instead of Plasma Cannon in those slots
Guardian has Derelict tag which forces it to use ballistic-centred skill instead of an energy one. Which makes it incompatible with Plasma Cannon.
Guardians will still equip Plasma Cannons by accident, as autofit has been turned on for them. But it will now be common for them to wield Mjolnir instead

Hegemony file has been completely replaced
Hegemony will no longer prioritise Condors and Moras. They will now spec into Legions first and foremost. This has been done to help them differentiate from other factions now that carriers will be more common. It also exists to seemingly reflect on their lore of Domain being quite ignorant of carrier doctrines
Additionally Hegemony will no longer prioritise Ballistic Mastery on their officers. As many ships in their fleet now use energy weapons. Apogee, Wolf. And Onslaught which now deals majority of its damage with TPCs with meaningful flux costs
The previous change to their doctrine being number focused has been reverted. And they are now back to spamming high level officers

Gave Hegemony Sarissa wing. This wing will most likely be never equipped but it can be now bought from them

Gave Hegemony 1 in phase ships doctrine causing them to use phase ships more often. I understand that phase ships in vanilla were still used by Hegemony due to faction file magic. But I want them to use even more phase ships now that Grendels and Gremlins are more effective

Gave GCR Warthog, Hoplon, Piranha and Sarissa Wing. Note that they will not use them, because uniquely enough they have priority in other wings. They however might sell them
Gave CGR more carriers in their doctrine

Made Persean League cruiser-focused instead of capital ship spam

Gave Pirates more phase ships and less warships.

Made Scavengers Steady doctrine instead of aggressive/reckless. This has been done as scavenger would often suicide their fleet into yours for no reason. Causing boring combat engagements. Now they will behave more opportunistically
Increased Scavengers' officer strength and reduced numbers.
This has been done to prevent enormous Scavenger fleets from spawning. As such large fleets would logically need too many supplies to sustain their weight
Reduced the change of combat freighters in their fleets.
Large swarms of combat freighters in scavenger fleets made them too akin to pirates. They would also be too easy to kill due to completely lacking damage. As most combat freighters have support roles instead of core ones

Restored Sindrian Diktat selling plenty of Phase Charge Launchers. As with the new Fury variant they now need more of them. And these weapons are fun to use and can't be bought anywhere else except from them or Tri-Tachyon

Completely replaced Tri-Tachyon file to remove the priority for them to put Energy Weapons Mastery on every ship. This has been done to prevent Tri-Tachyon from spawning abominable mercenary officers with both Energy Weapons Mastery and Ballistic Weapons Mastery. And also make up for the fact that certain ships do not really need Energy Weapons Mastery and rely on systems or missiles instead. Examples include the new Assault Fury variant, Omen, Tempest to a certain extent or Astral
Increased the amount of Carriers and reduced the amount of phase ships.
Carriers originally were set to 0 in Tri-Tachyon file, but due to Astral being prioritised they still spawned. VERY RARELY HOWEVER. Making it very difficult to actually see an Astral being sold on the market.
Reduced the amount of phase ships in Tri-Tachyon fleets, as phase ships aren't really a ship that does well when spammed in this mod due to there existing a lot of fighters now. Phase ships will still appear often enough in Tri-Tachyon fleets to be noticed. They will no longer however form half their combat lineup. Instead 33% of it


The complete list of balance changes in 2A patch:
SpoilerIn response to criticism, the „Difficulty Tweak” mod has been completely overhauled in terms of content. Again. For the 4th time. Additionally, in order to accommodate every player, a comprehensive patch note has been prepared to explain what has changed. Starting from the very beginning.

Raised the price of all commodities in the game by the factor of 2 to compensate for increased travel speed. And encourage players picking up junk from space to sell it on the market

Reduced penalty when all hostile to 50% instead of 100%. This will cause markets to be more difficult to exploit passively. Thus making it harder to profit from hostilities. And pirates and Pathers being incompetent

Made Farming as expensive as Aquaculture industry. This was done because Farming is the most profitable industry in the game. Especially with the introduction of Gilead crisis

Removed Population & Infrastructure upkeep. Halved the income of Population & Infrastructure. This has been done to make it simpler to inhabit planets with high hazard rating
(Population & Infrastructure has upkeep of farming but no income. Tech-Mining now has the income equivalent to old Population & Infrastructure income to incentivise keeping this industry around in spite of meagre gains)
This has been reworked in patch 2A-b

Removed Tech-mining upkeep. Tech-Mining now has an income equal to 10% of the original Population & Infrastructure income. This has been done to make it easier for players to harvest resources of planets in spite of incoming in this mod to be described economical changes
Also reworked in patch 2A-b

Refining and Light Industry upkeep swapped. This has been done because Light Industry earns no money. Whilst Refining earns a ton

Best of the Best no longer grants the control the battlefield passive. This has been done along also in this mod balance changes to encourage investing into other aspects of the game than 3 s-modded ships
Support Doctrine no longer reduces the DP cost of all unofficered ships by 20%. Ditto but with passive fleet strength increase

Electronic Warfare no longer grants the longer range and increased capture rate passive. This feature has been removed cause it's bugged and causes issue in NPC behaviour. It also causes capturing points very *** when enemies have it

Phase Corps no longer grants peak operating time bonus. The higher peak operating time is now built into the ships themselves

System Expertise and Missile Specialization are now accessible only after 2 skill points instead of 4. Additional points to acquire the second tier 2 skill are also 2 instead of 4

Neural Link and Automated Ships have swapped tiers. Neural Link hullmods no longer require ordnance points to be used. This has been done because automated ships were greatly nerfed in this mod. And the player should no longer need a high investment cap stone to acquire them. Note Radiant is accessible now. Keep reading for more information. Neural Link on the other hand has been buffed but also moved, because it's a very gimmicky and powerful character skill that officers a lot of versatility for a person that invests a lot of time into it. This does however make it greatly incompatible with Cybernetic Augmentation

Changed Derelict Operations flavour text to reflect that they are exclusively used by Derelicts. More of a passion project thing, I guess...

Doubled the minimum and max amount of bar events. The multiplier responsible for bar events is now 50% higher. This simply means you will now be able to more easily grab missions from planets instead of being forced to roam around in search of them. And being cursed with making friends with random people you hate

Combat speed is now 40% faster by default. This has been done to make the pace of the game faster. Please do not be confused as to why everything is so fast now

Combat readiness loss for weapon refit if not docked is now twice as little. And combat readiness loss for changing hullmods is now four times as little

Fighter crew losses are now 50% higher. Fighters have been greatly buffed in this mod with improvements to small weapons. This is why this has been changed

Max fleet size for retreat is now 300 instead of 150

Clean disengage numbers are now twice as little. Meaning it will be easier to retreat from a large fleet if found in a difficult situation

Hostile activity max monthly progress is now twice as little. Max amount of hostile activity fleets that can be in your system passively is 4 instead of 11

Station deployment bonus is now 4 instead of 1. Meaning it will be more difficult to have your  fleet locked out of defending a station due to the lack of objectives. This also means fighting over stations might now involve 600 DP worth of fleets beating the bees out of each other

Blueprint price for items is now equivalent to times 10 the original item cost instead of times 1.5. This applies for blueprints of items other than ships. For example the blueprint for Planetary Shield

Blueprint price for ships is now 10 times as high that of the original ship instead 0.5 as high. This means Paragon blueprint is now worth over 7 million credits on the Black Market
(THIS HAS BEEN REDUCED TO ONLY 5 TIMES. MEANING PARAGON WILL GO FOR ONLY 3.5 MILLION)

The default potential contact chance has been decreased by a factor of 5. The maximum amount of contacts you can have is now 2. This has been done to reflect on the general anxiety and loneliness of living in modern times

The minimum amount of missions a contact might have will now be 3 instead of 1. And maximum 6 instead of 3.

The price of weapons sold is now 100% instead of 50%. This means selling weapons will be extremely profitable

Colony items now can be sold for 10 times their price. Encouraging players to sell them if they find them early on. Buying them back will cost additional 50% of the price they were sold for

Ships sold on the market now cost 100% of their original price instead of 120%. The player sells these ships for 100% of their value instead of 40%. Let that sink in

D-modded ship price multiplier is now 50% instead of 20%. This applies to both selling and buying ships. Meaning you can sell your garbage for a little profit instead of scavenging it

Base system bounty (the one given by systems when they are under siege) is now 5k per ship, instead of 1k. The amount of system bounties has been increased from 0 min and 3 max to 1 min and 5 max

Base player Commerce industry bounty is now 2k instead of 0.5k

Pirate, Pather and person bounties have been increased in pay by a factor of 4. Passive bounties are now more rare. You can visit bars though to find them. This has been done to make the setting more realistic in that you wouldn't expect the Sector to be passively patrolled by endless renegades

Pirate and Pather bases are now more common:
Minimum amount of pirate bases (the number of bases that the game will try to boost into existence) is now 5 instead of 2. Maximum (the maximum amount of pirate bases that there can be in the Persean Sector) is now 10 instead of 3.
Minimum and maximum Pather base numbers are now twice as high. Going from 2 min and 3 max to 4 min and 6 maximum.
The base rate at which these bases grow is now still small, contrary to the initial release of this mod. When it was extremely high. Meaning that you will find a lot of pirate and Pather bases. But they will be non-threatening as long as you clear them out before they grow

Raid defender increase numbers have been fixed. Causing this mechanic to now work properly. Repeatedly raiding the same planet will greatly increase its defence against the player. This mechanic is strong even for the weakest colonies

Cost of bombing planets is now twice as high in fuel. Meaning you will need twice as much fuel as the colony has defences instead of a number equal to them. There has been no additional tampering to bombing mechanics contrary to initial release of this mod

The strength of NPC raiding is now 100% stronger. This does apply most importantly to pirate raids. Other than that it does not affect the strength of expeditions. Merely their ability to raid your colony. This mechanic used to be far more important when factions were capable of sending expeditions to raid your colonies. This mechanic has not been restored. Thus it now only applies to pirates. As Pathers bomb your colonies instead. This translates to pirate raids causing a much greater stability loss

Faction commission bounty is now 2k per ship, instead of 0.3k. Base pay is 20k with 5k increase per level instead of reverse. Resigning the commission will now affect the player with a -100 reputation loss instead of -10. When done in person the loss will be only -50 instead of -5. This greatly increases the amount of money you get from hunting down pirates and enemies of the faction. Whereas in vanilla it was mostly a waste of time

The restoration of peaceful relations between hostile nations penalty is now -5 instead of -10. This means you will no longer become hostile to the Hegemony over time simply because Andrada's lackeys kept declaring war on it every other Tuesday. And then getting peace back again every other Thursday. Unless you choose to maul them

The probability of hostilities between nations is now twice as little. This on top of the previous change means having a commission is far less annoying. And encouraged even to acquire ships and weapons from factions. It's not however uncommon enough to not be problematic. Hostilities still happen regularly. It's just that in vanilla they happened constantly to the point of ridiculousness in my opinion

Distress calls now have global range creating an atmosphere of hopelessness in the Sector. Getting to them is now far more difficult. This has been done more as flavour. In vanilla they were too close thus making the player FEEL like they have to go to them. Now it's something you can do if you have a nimble fleet and feel like being charitable. This is technically a huge nerf to the mechanic. But a nerf that might add some gameplay complexity and player choice

D-mod restore multiplier is now 110% instead of 120%. Meaning repairing broken ships is now cheaper. This has been done because the player will now be more impoverished in general

Weapons now have a 25% chance of being lost when a ship is destroyed. (this feature has been removed) Chance of finding weapons from killed enemies is now 50% higher. This does also apply to Omega enemies. Meaning you will recover 75% of weapons of the enemies you kill

Fighter wings have now a 25% chance of being lost when a ship is destroyed. The chance of finding fighter wings on killed enemies is now 200% higher

The chance of finding a hullmod from killed enemies is now 400% higher

NOTE THAT WITH THESE BALANCE CHANGES YOU WILL NOW EARN MORE MONEY FROM KILLING PEOPLE. FIRST RULE OF IR PULSE LASER SAFETY IS HAVING FUN

Max ship gain from doctrine is 3 instead of 1.5. Meaning the sector will now have twice as many ships which you can fight and buy. This has been done to balance fleet doctrines a bit better. To elaborate. This means that with every faction doctrine increase, the fleet size will grow by 40%. Up to a 200% increase in the amount of ships deployed. This translates to pirate fleets being huge. But it mostly translates to being a lot more ships in general

Quality gain per fleet doctrine point is now 25% instead of 12.5%. Penalty from imports is now 10% instead of 25%. There will be now higher quality ships in the sector in general. This has been done to encourage putting points into quality. As in vanilla quality was pretty much a joke stat that meant nothing in the long run. If at all

The maximum amount of mercenary fleets is now twice as high. Meaning Core World systems are now more likely to have random independent murders lurking about. This has been done to counter the pirate prevalence a bit. But generally it is a non-noticeable change

Player max level reduced from 15 to 12. Story points per level is now 2 instead of 4. This is an extremely controversial change that has been done to prevent the player from making all the mechanics in the game irrelevant. I'll admit character skills were often my least favourite part of Starsector. Individual ship optimisation and skill-expression. Commanding fleets. As well as building up colonies. All these things are often made irrelevant by the incredible power of having something like Electronic Warfare, Support Doctrine, Phase Coil Tuning, Crew Training, Coordinated Maneuvers, etc. At the same time. Certain skills have been nerfed. As mentioned at the beginning of this post. This has been done to create some meta variety. Generally ships are more responsive due to the power of weapons increasing. It just means that non-amplified ships will feel stronger. You also level up officers faster. So you can shift your strategies incredibly quickly. Multiple times through your playthrough. I'm really sorry if this balance change doesn't fit your attitude towards the game. But it has been done to increase difficulty. Yes. There is no other explanation behind that. I didn't do it out of malice. I did it, because I felt it would make Starsector experience more fair towards NPCs. And thus it would allow me to nerf them where necessary to maintain gameplay integrity. Prevent power creep and such? You know? Whatever...

Officers now level up 8 4 times as fast

Lowered the maximum level required for fleet commanders to have both fleet-boosting admiral skills. This will cause lesser fleets to be more dangerous

Doubled crew, marine and officer PER LEVEL salary. Each crew costs 20 credits. Each marine costs 40. Each level of an officer costs additional 800 instead of 10, 20 and 400. The base officer salary remains the same at 500 credits. This change has been done to add more passive spending to the game. It's not severe enough to make you completely paralysed economically (AS IT WAS BEFORE IN THIS MOD FOR WHICH I APOLOGISE). Even though realistically it should. Note Invictus has been rebalanced to prevent this from becoming ridiculous. Also note that with more ships, more weapons and more money from bounties. You should still be able to stay afloat as long as you kill a lot of people

Doubled the chance of finding officers and merc officers on colonies. As well as having the chance to promote one after combat. The merc chance is especially important. As it will allow you to stack more competence at your side as long as you have the money to do it. Contrary to vanilla in which money didn't exist. And the only restrictor was the extreme rarity of merc officers to the point of it being really frustrating. And also making players sad about bullying an officer into staying in your army for the rest of your life

Doubled the values of base burn and storm strike burn speed. Meaning travel will now be ridiculously fast for all fleets in the game. This does not affect actual ship stats. This translates to expeditions and raids arriving sooner. Missions being completed faster and the pace of  gameplay being incredibly fast. You are no longer going to have to listen to twelve hours of podcasts when waiting for your fleet to get somewhere. Btw. This does mean you can use a Black Hole to launch yourself across the entire Persean Sector.

Increased the cost of FP per AI Core by a factor of 2. Making swarms of Alpha Cores uncommon. The swarms of Alpha Cores is what I would consider the most *** mechanic in the game. Nerfing this is the most important aspect that allows for the nerfing of player character long-termly without making the game incredibly challenging. This along Remnant ship changes has made Remnants a more believable threat to the Hegemony. Rather than a godlike entity that the player is amazed at the fact that they didn't eat the whole Persean Sector in a week. This does not affect Derelict bounties. As they use a separate hard-coded AI core assignment mechanic.

Reduced base sensor profile from 300 to 100. Reworked sensor scaling per ship size from 30->60->90->150 to 20->40->80->160. The maximum amount of ships affecting sensor profile is now 10. This means small fleets will be invisible, deaf and blind. And large ones will be easily seen and aware of their surroundings. This greatly decreases the difficulty of smuggling missions and others. But makes sneaking around large fleets as a large fleet incredibly difficult. If you are having problems with finding stuff in a star system. I recommend you use something other than 2 Wolves and a Hound. If your fleet has 2 Atlases (militarised), 5 Ventures (militarised), and 3 Falcons. Your fleet profile is now 980. In vanilla it would be 700. And this isn't even your final form. You can go up to 1700 excluding sensor multipliers like the "I see you, little fish" passive. If you are having trouble with this mechanic, then skill issue tbh...

Increased escape and flanking distance in retreat scenarios making it more likely to evade heavier ships whilst using frigates to intercept escapees in such scenarios. This is extremely important to be honest. But will rarely be talked about due to such scenarios being rare. However with limited s-points it was necessary. You will still however get surrounded and die quite easily if you are against a swarm of pirates that will deploy 20 Cerberi on your face

The amount of DP both fleets need for the objectives to spawn is now 200 instead of 100. Meaning low level encounters will now be harder to control by easily grabbing objectives. And the player might actually be locked from deploying their entire fleet. This has been done due to objectives being generally boring when there are not enough ships to contest them regularly through combat

Emergency repair DP value was increased by 50%. Meaning you can repair more ships using this campaign scenario

Historian s-point cost to find item is now 1 instead of 4. And the amount to improve industry is now 1 instead of 2. Note both these values double per each usage as in vanilla. This has been done to compensate for increased industry upkeep and s-point nerfs

Immigration penalty per hazard is now twice as high. The amount of growth points needed to ascend towards a higher colony level is now 3 times the vanilla value. The amount of credits need for a singular point of immigration is now 5 times as high. (this particular nerf has been removed) However Hazard Pay now brings immigration to 20 40 instead of 5 points. Meaning growing colonies is more expensive but more dynamic. Generally far quicker if it comes from going to 4 from 3. But far slower when you are trying to build massive colonies out of nothing on horrible planets

Industry upkeep cost is 100% higher than vanilla. This has been done along the previous change because players are generally able to very quickly assemble colonies. This is a huge issue in vanilla balancing, because it allows players to rapidly print money out of thin air. They quickly become the strongest entity in the Persean Sector. Causing the Core Worlds to become a joke. And making the dev introduce ridiculous mechanics to compensate for that. The ridiculous mechanics have been removed or nerfed now. So, now the only enemy of yours is the fact that you are broke. Making for a more realistic fringe inhabiting scenario. This change is meant to exist in conjunction with a mod that doesn't exist yet. So, please take them with a grain of salt. And feel free to complain

Tech-Mining Decay is 50% slower. This change is generally unnoticeable to be honest. Tech-Mining now at least doesn't cost money now. It only costs an industry slot

Over max industries penalty is now 5 instead of 10. Affects only Hypershunt and Sat Bombed colonies that were not wiped out

Admin salary and hiring costs are now 4 times as little. You can now have 5 admins. The idle admin salary is now 2 times as little as vanilla value. This has been done, because the upkeep increase does feel a bit strong

You can now manage industry items on colonies remotely from any place in the Persean Sector

Advanced Turret Gyros s-mod now works up. You can now use it on a frigate to increase its damage against Capital Ships

ECCM Package s-mod effect no longer exists. This has been done because flares have been buffed. And form an important part in campaign against strong missiles. ECCM ignoring flares and Electronic Warfare would be ridiculously overpowered in the current system and impossible to balance. The hullmod costs a generic amount anyway that does not allow for the existence of a strong s-mod effect

Expanded Mags s-mod buff is now 25% faster ammo regen instead of 50%. This is a huge nerf that I have brought upon thee because I hate Storm Needler. But Storm Needler no longer exists so. Whatever... 25% is still a lot. But it will probably be now one of the least used s-mods in the game in this mod

Front-Shield Conversion now gives 30% additional shield profile instead of 100%. Wholly covered ships were broken and are broken in vanilla. This nerf has been given to encourage Accelerated and Extended Shields. Instead of cheap... Freaking... BS Front-Shield Conversion hullmod. You can still use it on a Paragon to give it faster deployment. But it is now as viable as Omni-Shield Conversion. A flavour tool, to say the least

High Scatter Amplifier now works past 400 range instead of 200. Beam weapons were reworked however. More on that later. For now all you need to know is that getting into 600 range with a Phase Lance (yes, Phase Lance now has 800) isn't what it used to be

Ill-Advised is no longer a d-mod. Meaning you can’t fix it from a ship. But the chance of it occurring is now 5 times less likely. This has been done to prevent Pathers from being useless. The Safety Overrides were nerfed. A bit. Yes. And buffed at the same time. But it also means you can pick up a Pather ship and use it without having half your arsenal break instantly

Safety Overrides no longer gives passive movement speed bonus. Its range reduction now applies after 600 units instead of 450. It now reduces peak operating time by a factor of 2 instead of 3. Can now be equipped by civilian, capital ships. And ships with Flux Shunt. Safety overrides are generally one of the most debated hullmods in the game. I disagree that they are overpowered as much. As some people explain. I also disagree that we should rework it into some sort of an incredibly complex gimmick. This is because there are a lot of people who like them for what they are. I did nerf the system eventually. Cause it did feel *** a bit. Especially with 600 Chaingun range and 640 DPS HMG. But it is still strong. Very strong... Just in a different way. And you can now put it on an Invictus.

Shield Shunt reworked. Now grants 40% fire rate at the penalty of 20% increased flux spending on weapons. Does not affect missile weaponry. So, no. You can’t use it with *** green missiles. I’m looking at you [NAME REDACTED]. S-mod bonus armour increased from 15% to 20%. The original value was 15% but it stacked with base armour increase of 15%. Ending up at 30%.
This has been done because Shield Shunt in vanilla is either useless or overpowered as hell. And this attempts to push it towards a different direction to avoid the issue entirely.

Converted Hangar can no longer be built-in. Converted Hangar op cost is now 0.

Andrada Mods are no longer a d-mod and can’t be fixed. Andrada ships no longer suffer from an OP penalty. Executor no longer has 0.6 shields. This huge nerf has been done because Executor with missile and beam changes is now an extremely powerful ship that felt *** to fight. It did get some OP to compensate I guess

Talon’s turning is now twice as responsive. Talon’s firing angle has been increased from 0 to 90. Greatly increasing its intercepting capabilities. This has been done to make it more on par with Wasp with incoming to be described PD Laser changes

Trident’s flux dissipation is now twice as high of that of a normal High Tech bomber or fighter. This only affects the amount of time it spends overloaded and its durability against beam weapons

Warthog’s Insulated Engine Assembly hullmod removed. Flux stats doubled. Now has ammofeed instead of flares. Warthog's slow movement speed makes it incompatible with the role of an escort fighter. So it now fully embraces its damage dealing potential. As Light Mortar has also been greatly buffed

Thunder turning responsiveness is now twice as high. This change has been taken from a forum post: https://fractalsoftworks.com/forum/index.php?topic=30961.msg453901#msg453901

Wasp is now 3 second respawn time. Also taken from the same post

Doubled Broadsword flux stats. This has been done because with increase to PD weapons strength that is also in this mod. As well as nerfs to flares. Broadsword is now far more vulnerable

Decreased the durability of fighter flares by reducing their health from 500 to 200. This paired with PD changes, means a PD Laser shoots down a flare in 1.33 seconds

Gladius now has twice as high flux stats and uses Damper instead of flares. This has been done to make it more unique rather than just deploying flares to confuse enemies. Visually it feels pretty nicely tbh

Sarissa’s durability reduced to that of a Gladius fighter. Previously was as tough as a Warthog. Given Ballistic Rangefinder to compensate
Xyphos shield durability is now 300 flux instead of 600. This along Sarissa nerf has been done because escort fighters are generally kinda bs to fight. I did not add them into fleet doctrines of factions. Although I should have to just prove a point. You will only see Xyphos on that one Aurora variant. But having long-ranged extremely durable, easy to recover swarms of spammy fighters is incredibly frustrating. Converted Hangar has been buffed to compensate

Terminator Drone's durability is now that of a Claw without a shield. Previously as tough as Broadsword with 33% less hull durability. Terminator sequence damage now does 100% more energy and EMP damage. Range is now 1200 instead of 1500 causing less confusion for NPCs. As it would often be used prematurely causing it to be wasted. The wing rebirth timer is now 15 seconds instead of 20. This has been done because Terminator Drone having high damage now justifies losing PD for a moment. But the reduction of hull durability and armour for a fighter means that the missile can be shot down before connecting. Though it'll be hard due to high mobility stats of the fighter

Hound, Vanguard, Gremlin, Cerberus, Mudskipper, Wayfarer durability increased by 1k hull points and 150 armour. And adjusted their PTS stats for them to spawn more consistently. This has been done because these early game enemies were always a joke. They had no roles and were thrown into the trash as soon as possible. They only existed to make the player feel good in the early game just to crush their self-esteem with Remnants in the late game. They are now viable. Note that Wayfarer is 5 DP. It's as expensive as a Wolf. And yet it was the most crap piece of garbage ship in the game that you wouldn't consider using even if it was 4 DP. Now it's worth something. It's a tanky piece of crap. Very neat. Especially with buffed missiles and flares

Pirate Mudskipper now has Heavy Ballistic Integration and no longer suffers from Ill-Advised Modifications. Fixing the Mudskipper MKII will now create a normal Mudskipper. Adjusted PTS stats for it to spawn far more commonly. Ditto

Hyperion now has 50 op instead of 80. Costs 10 DP and has 60 degrees less shield profile. The ship now costs only 20 supplies per month instead of 40. Increased peak operating time to 180 seconds. And adjusted PTS stats for them to spawn more commonly
With nerfed s-point gains, less character skills, and stronger fighters and missile weapons. Hyperion now embraces the role of a tactical frigate that exploits the situation when it is not hard-countered. Instead of being a gimmicky ship that some people prided themselves in being able to use

Lowered Afflictor’s DP cost to 8. Shade’s to 6. Increased peak operating time to 300 seconds. Same reasons as Hyperion. Phase ships in general have been a really garbage tier level of ships that were only used by a select group of people. They will still be that. But these people now at least will finally be happy because their ships will no longer be an incredibly difficult to use gimmick that brings the same rewards as using a Paragon does. Except with 10 times more calories spent on making things work out instead of being dumb

Lowered Scarab’s DP to 6. Scarab dies easily and is limited in mobility and weapons. Vanguard and other junk ships have been increased in power. So Scarab can now join them without feeling overpowered

Warden, Defender, Picket, Sentry durability increased by 1500 hull points and 150 armour points. Max speed increased by 50. Mobility greatly increased. Adjusted PTS stats for them to spawn in greater numbers. Derelicts are now incredibly dangerous and difficult to shut down contrary to their vanilla form of being nothing but a joke like other early game enemies. They are not immortal however. And are vulnerable to EMP, HIL and other proper anti-armour solutions. Especially considering many of them were buffed in this mod

Gremlin is now 5 DP and has canister_flak instead of fighter flares system. Increased peak operating time to 300 seconds. Ditto as for Shade and Afflictor

Adjusted Centurion, Brawler, Vigilance PTS stats for them to spawn in greater numbers. These ships had unfairly high PTS values in ship_data.csv causing them to make fleets that utilised them significantly weaker than fleets that didn't bother and just spammed Falcons. Only affects NPCs

TT Brawler now costs 6 DP. With buffed beams and other energy weapons. TT Brawler with its plasma jets is now unstoppable. And from what I heard it always has been. So, now it is unstoppable unstoppable

SO Brawler now costs 5 DP, because Ill-Advised modifications can no longer be removed

Kite is now twice as cheap. Shepherd requires less crew to run. This has been done to make the early game less painful

Reworked Fortress Shield. Now can last only up to 10 seconds and has 3 seconds cooldown. This has been done to make Paragon and Monitor less oppressive. Paragon changes will be talked about later

Monitor has received twice as high flux stats to compensate. Monitor is now kinda good, but also dies easily. It's a sane ship that is worth 6 DP and it will die easily if pressured. Making it a proper escort ship now

Enforcer PTS stats adjusted for same reasons as Brawler, Vigilance, Centurion were. This has most likely been done originally in the game because Enforcer is extremely tanky. Tanky vessels like Vanguard, Centurion and even Invictus get disproportionally higher PTS values to make the game less time-consuming. This has been undone and rebalanced with stronger missile weapons, more damage in energy ones and faster combat speed instead in this mod

Condor has now 55 OP instead of 45. Increased peak operating time. Condor can now use bombers without having a stroke. And even equip Expanded Missile Racks to snipe frigates from across the field. 10/10 ship now

Gemini now has now 90 OP instead of 85. And now costs 8 DP. PTS value adjusted to make it spawn more often. Gemini is generally a piece of trash. But now it might be a viable piece of trash. Who knows?

Increased Buffalo2’s durability by 2250 hull durability and 200 armour. This means Buffalo MKII is has almost as much hull durability as the Enforcer. For 4 DP, it can pursue frigates relentlessly and make them waste a ton of time. It still costs a lot of crew to run. And is generally easy to kill. But if approached with wrong weapons. It can use its flares to discredit missiles. Emanate a lot of influence. Etc.

Mule is now 6 DP. Its cost is now 17k instead of 34k. Mule is now kinda weak. Always has been. And it has been expensive too. With increased strength of frigates and missile strength, it's now easier to kill. Thus it has been made cheaper and simpler to deploy

Sunder now has 400 armour instead of 250. This has been done due to weapon changes that have made it obsolete. More on that later... But basically with increased ballistic range and decreased beam range. Sunder struggles to survive. With bonus armour it still will die very easily. But at least it'll stand a chance if caught off guard. If not caught off guard, it's the strongest ship in the game atm. And that's a good thing. And if you disagree... Well... Too bad

Harbinger is now 14 DP. Costs twice as little. PTS stat adjusted for it to be more common. Now has 480 seconds peak operating time. This has been done for the same reasons as Shade and Afflictor

Shrike has now 10 additional max speed. PTS stats adjusted for it to spawn more commonly. Shrike now dies way more easily to due to increased missile strength and ballistic weapons strength. In vanilla 105 speed is enough to dodge most threats. But the buggy microburn AI causes it to blow up randomly for no reason. It's kinda funny... In this mode Shrike will die very easily. But with 115 speed, it can be extremely ridiculous if it comes to flanking, capping points, chasing down frigates. Etc. Especially considering energy weapons changes and missile strength increase

Bastillon and Berserker have received 1.25k more hull durability and 300 more armour. Their speed is now 20 units higher and their mobility has been drastically increased. For the same reason as previous Derelicts like Defender. Bastillon especially now is a quite fearsome adversary that with its 500 range Vulcans and annoyingly good at catching missiles flares will shut down most missile presence temporarily until blown up

Falcon is now 15 DP and has 350 flux venting instead of 400
Eagle is now 22 DP and has 600 flux venting instead of 700
These two ships in my opinion were power crept in the game, because of the refusal to properly address energy weapons being bad. They have been reverted as in this mod energy weapons are now extremely powerful. And Eagle having almost as much flux venting as Aurora and way more than Champion in spite of costing 5 DP less felt really weird

Venture is now 130 OP. Pirate Venture no longer receives an OP penalty. Pather Venture now has SO. The respawn timer of mining drones is now 5 seconds instead of 10. With increased missile strength, Ventures will now die very easily. In vanilla they are also considered really bad because of their extremely boring gameplay. With additional OP and increased drone numbers. They will be able to perform adequately and help where possible.
Pather and pirate Venture buffs on the other hand are meant to make gameplay more challenging. These ships are very rare anyway

Eradicator now costs 20 DP instead of 22. Pirate one is now 16 DP. Eradicator imo is an underpowered boring ship in vanilla Starsector. With these changes it can now finally claim its rightful destiny. And we don't have to worry about it becoming a spam of Velociraptors and Maulers cause they have been indirectly nerfed by buffing all the other ballistic weapons of that calibre

Fury now has 10 more max movement speed. PTS stats adjusted for them to spawn more commonly. For the same reasons as Shrike

Drover no longer has b-deck. Drover now uses Reserve Deployment instead of Active Flares. Drover in its current state is the worst carrier in the game. Even though it was already kinda bad in previous patches. It was nerfed, because it was one of the few still viable carriers and let alone destroyers the game had to offer. As a vengeful letter to the ambivalent universe. I give thee a 14 DP carrier with as many wings as Legion

Aurora is now 25 DP. Aurora suffers a lot from increased strength of ballistics in this mod. It generally is also extremely expensive and rare. With additional heavy nerf to Front-Shield Conversion it will have to rely on spending its amogus humongous OP budget on stuff like Extended Shields. Less s-mods also means less potency

Apogee now has 150 OP, 0.6 shield efficiency and costs 18 DP. Apogee has been nerfed to the ground because it used to be one of the few spammable easy to use High Tech ships. Which was obviously wrong for reasons we do not fully understand. Now it's again spammable. But it will die quickly to ballistic spam. Its flares however are really powerful now

Active and non-active flare attraction range and chance doubled

Doom is now 40 DP. Its mine strike now does twice as much damage. Peak operating time now 600. This ridiculous change has been done for the same reason as Afflictor and Shade. Except it's reverse. Instead of the ship receiving a simple number change. It has received a stronger system. This is to make the bombs more reasonable in appearance. As to why does such a big bomb deal so little damage? And also to somewhat prevent Doom from being an obnoxious anti-fighter counter. It now instead counters everything. As it should be

Grendel now 22 DP. No longer suffers from the inability to equip ITU. Given 20 more OP to be able to equip it. The hullmod that gave Grendel bonus durability against EMP is now gone. The ship is now free to become a long-range artillery unit that utilises phase to the extreme. To be honest, I have to admit something. When I read the description of this ship. I kinda imagine myself. I feel like I'm the stupid admiral that has secured part of the sector to make creatures beyond comprehension. Things that are absolutely hateful and devoid of happiness. Things that eat away the body and soul. Mind. And belch forward... Abominations absolute. So, buffing this ship has been a quite person matter. Not going to lie. Thank you, Alex and David for making this. I know we most likely have completely different views of what proper balancing is. Which makes me extra glad that I can mod it to whatever I want it to be

Heron now has 115 OP instead of 100. Increased peak operating time to 420 from 360. Heron can now equip ITU without feeling bad. This has been done in an effort to generally increase the strength of carriers in the game and make them feel less restricted

Mora now has 140 OP instead of 125. Increased peak operating time to 480. Ditto as for Heron

Colossus crew requirements halved. Costs less PTS. Both variants are now 8 DP. This has been done to make Colossus appear less comical in nature. Killing one and being able to dispose of so many pirates at once feels like it would make the faction rapidly run out of troops. Now it makes slightly more sense

Rampart hull durability increased to 15k and armour to 1750. Max speed is now 40 instead of 35. With increase to the power of HIL, missiles, etc. Rampart now dies very easily. It has received a huge durability upgrade to make up for its lacking speed and OP adaptability. Feel free to get one with the Automated Fleets character skill

Onslaught DP cost increased to 50. Now has 800 flux venting instead of 600. Onslaught generally is overpowered imo. But nerfing it directly would feel cruel to the people who have mastered it. With 800 DP and new Storm Needler. A XIV variant can now actually duel unoptimised Paragons. So be afraid when you see one. It now costs 50 DP. But it can now fire away all its weapons without overfluxing as quickly

Atlas MKII DP cost decreased to 20. Prometheus MKII to 25. These ships will now die very easily to bombers and missiles. HIL too. They are very threatening nonetheless. And they should be. They will now form a proper challenge throughout the entirety of the game. And not only because of Squall and Hurricane spam. Or some other gimmick. They are now simply put... Incredibly strong and spammable. Yes. On the other hand they are also incredibly slow and lacking in durability. So if you have a capital ship like Invictus, Onslaught, Paragon. Or anything of that size. Even Dominator will do. You should be able to wipe them out one by one with no issues. KINDA

Astral now has 300 OP. 22k base flux capacity. Recall Device now has a 10 second cooldown. This is a buff and a nerf. With more flux capacity Astral will now take more flux to use its system. 11 thousand flux to be precise. So make sure to spec that OP into additional venting and Stabilised Shields hullmod

Conquest now has a 1.2 shield. Conquest has always been underpowered. This is why I buffed it. Duh

Odyssey now has 290 instead of 280 OP. And a 0.8 shield. For the same reason. Battleships in the game generally have a shield weaker by 0.2 units by default. On top of huge PD and shape restrictions. With increased missile strength. Conquest and Odyssey will now be in far more pain overall.

Paragon now has 1500 flux venting to make up for the loss of Fortress Shield indefiniteness and spammability traits. Additionally Paragon is now extremely vulnerable to new kinetics, missiles, fighters. Etc. It deserves to be the strongest ship in the game. So I'm removing its greatest restriction, whilst at the same time taking away its biggest strength. Kinda funny

Legion has now 320 OP. XIV variant 330. Hegemony has regained its XIV variant. Legion was given more OP as in an attempt to make carriers more versatile. Hegemony has been given back Legion XIV... For long-term balance testing purposes

Invictus hull durability is 20k. Lidar cooldown is now 20 seconds. Logistical costs of crew requirements, mass, max crew and base cost have been halved. DP is now 50. Name changed to Unconquered. Cause calling it that is the equivalent of calling Onslaught „Impetus”. Description unchanged. Meaning LC members are free to call it Invictus. Yes, I’m a TT main, how can you tell :3
Additionally it has been given pre nerf flux stats.
This has been done because Invictus being a giant immobile immortal brick is kinda boring in terms of gameplay. Additionally Invictus has been given a do_not_back_off hidden hullmod that will cause it to act incredibly aggressively, so that its AI issues related to its low armour stats are fixed.. With lower DP. More damage. Invictus will be in behaviour similar to an actual offensive attack ship of massive size. Rather than just... Nothing

Pegasus has 50 max speed again. With increases to PD, the Pegasus' ability to saturate the battlefield with missiles is no longer as uncounterable. ***. It now requires the attribute of mobility to make worth of its subjective arsenal paired with its high DP cost and low durability, and flux stats.

Retribution hull durability changed to 11k and armour to 1100. Shield strength changed to 1.2 and profile is now twice as wide. Retribution is a funni gimmick ship in vanilla that serves to make Harbingers good with Advanced Optics. In this mod it still will be that to some extent. But it will now have a way harder time going in and bombing stuff with Hephaestus AG

Guardian has now 1500 flux venting. No longer manufactures missiles. No longer has Advanced Targeting Unit. And has a shield of efficiency 1.4. Costs 60 DP. Can now be recovered. This has been done not to bully the player, but to make the Derelict bounties easier.
After buffing all the other Derelicts, the Guardian seemed like an incredible obnoxious knife serving as the cherry on top. It has been standardised. Making it as strong as a typical human 60 DP battleship. Those don't exist btw. So, it is a balance of durability, firepower, flux venting and an obnoxious hard to maintain ship. Something you would imagine to be an actual Derelict. Rather than a freaking... Self-insert boss. No offense. You can get it now btw. I assume it's fun

Derelict Mothership durability greatly increased as to prevent it from just randomly dying in a boss fight. Don't worry. It's still useless. It's just now really tough to kill

REMNANT CHANGES:

All Remnants now have 0.8 shields. Remnants have been reworked thoroughly to make them less obnoxious to fight. They will now depend on synergy. Aggressive tactics. The strength of AI cores to make their lives mean something

Remnant Battlestation now has 25% weaker shields
Damaged Remnant Battlestation will now have shields
It will no longer be as easy to just sneak in and steal an Alpha Core from a medium threat system. But Remnant stations will now no longer feel as *** with their incredible durability and firepower. Now they only have the firepower... And buffed fighters... And HIL that does 1k damage per second. And Gauss that does 500 DPS too... Uhhhhhhh...

Fulgent is now 10 DP and costs 40k instead of 50k. Fulgent no longer has Bolt Coherer. Max speed changed to 105 and mobility greatly increased, making it more akin to a large Glimmer or Lumen instead of a Sunder with two Reaper pods. Funnily enough this fits its description more.
The description talks about the ship being exceptionally mobile or something. And yet it's slower than a Hammerhead or Sunder. Reworking this ship makes it into a far more vulnerable Remnant actor that will easily destroy stuff if left to itself. It serves amazingly as an escort ship. Easily turning around and dodging projectiles. But due to it having 0.8 shields, it will die very easily if pressured. And it lacking range makes up for the fact that it has the highest firepower of any destroyer in the game with 2 medium missile launchers and 1 medium energy on top of other weapons it possesses

Scintilla now has b-deck.
I tried redesigning Remnant fighters to be less cumbersome in terms of respawn timers. But that would ultimately only take away what made them unique. So I gave Scintilla the removed in this mod Drover hullmod. It will now have extended stamina for prolonged combat encounters which paired with increased fighter strength to be discussed makes it extremely powerful

Brilliant no longer has microburn. Instead it has active flares and a hangar bay like it used to. Now costs 20 DP. Restored old description.
With this change Fulgent is now capable of countering average Cruisers in prolonged combat whilst being extremely vulnerable to larger threats. It forms a proper backline to Remnant fleets providing PD and long-range firepower. Serving the role Fulgent does in vanilla

Apex is now 25 DP.
With changes to Terminator drones and shield efficiency. Apex can now be 25 DP and roam the battlefield in all its glory. Tearing away enemies with incredible firepower as long as it is not shot at for too long. Causing it to break in half. Note that it along other Remnants have relatively high hull durability. So in spite of shields being weaker. It's not that easy to kill

Radiant flux venting reduced from 1500 to 1250
Nova shield profile doubled
Reckless AI paired with 0.8 shields makes these ships now far easier to catch off guard and kill. But note you will have less s-points and admiral skills to do so. Nova is now one of the easiest capital ships in the game to kill due to its suicidal behaviour. As always. But Radiant in spite of having lower flux venting and 0.8 shields will remain menacing as ever thanks to improved synergy with the rest of its fleet

END OF REMNANT CHANGES

EMP lightning does now twice as much damage.
Due to the fact that EMP does no damage. Players were inclined to use AMBs on Omens for majority of their firepower. This feels... Okay? But generally it's dumb. Omens would get stuck firing their EMP generator for days on random ships on the map, doing no damage. Now with increased strength of kinetic solutions and missiles. Omen will die very easily. So it was given an incredible boost to its DPS potential.

Piranha now has twice as many bombs. Their deployment is also 100% faster. Piranha positioning adjusted to make it not lag the entire bomber group. Same done for Longbow
Due to coordinated bombing that was introduced recently. Some bombers bug out in their behaviour and will refuse to fire missiles until extremely close to their target. So close, that Longbow will in fact ram the Sabot into the ship without it actually having enough time to detonate.
But focusing on Piranha. Piranha just needed more damage potential tbh. So, I gave it more. I probably should have buffed the projectile's damage instead. But this felt more appropriate considering changes made to Swarmer and Annihilator

Phase Charge Launcher old fire rate restored. Remnant bombers now use a standard Phase Charge Bomb Launcher with 5 bombs instead of a unique one that behaves weirdly. This also means they have been given spread.
(UNMENTIONED PREVIOUSLY REMNANT BOMBERS NOW HAVE 3 FIGHTERS PER WING INSTEAD OF 2 DUE TO DRAMATIC DAMAGE INCREASE)
Shrike and Fury strength was greatly reduced in an attempt to nerf Onslaught. Wait, what?
So, I nerfed the Onslaught to buff the Shrike.

LAG now does 50 damage per shot.
LAG being buffed is supposed to encourage buffing armoured enemies in the game like Vanguard or Defender. This specialist tool now actually does something. Just like HIL. It doesn't outdo a missile short-termly. But it does so long-termly. Infinite ammo... VERY HIGH DAMAGE. 200 HE DPS btw. And flux efficient... You are now encouraged to use it over Light Autocannon. Take that random flux efficiency buffs!

Light Mortar now fires twice as fast. This has been done to make the Light Mortar on par with LAG. Even though it costs 2 OP, it does spend a small ballistic slot. It needs to pull its weight. And lacklustre accuracy and projectile speed will make up for it

Arbalest, Heavy AC, Heavy Needler, Thumper, Heavy Mortar, LAG, Light Mortar, Light AC, Light Dual AC, Railgun, Light Needler have all been given additional 100 range. This has been done because energy weapons and missile weapons have been buffed. Additionally I have buffed Chaingun and HMG. Making it a weird choice between Heavy Mortar and Chaingun. Increased range isn't really that meaningful due to low projectile speed and poor accuracy. Meaning this change is only meaningful if ships have the right character skills.
This does also make it simpler for frigates, destroyers and lighter cruisers to fight against capital ships. Something like Enforcer or Eradicator benefits from this the most

Storm Needler now has 900 range, but fires at 40 flux efficiency and at old fire rate. And no longer uses ammo mechanics.
I really dislike the current state of Storm Needler. So I have reverted it to its old state with a minor buff and nerf to compensate. The current state of things makes it not stand out that much

Plasma Cannon now shoots projectiles that travel 33% slower. Deal twice as much damage. But fires them at twice as slow fire rate. Giving it same DPS at higher strength.
This has been mostly done because the size of the projectile was really confusing when compared to the actual damage it dealt. Plasma Cannon was also too generalist causing Odyssey with Plasma Cannon spam to be too oppressive ironically enough. So, bam... Nerfed?

Hephaestus AG now has old spread mechanics. Projectiles now do 150 HE damage at 120 flux cost.
This has been done because in its current vanilla state this gun feels really boring to use. It has no skill expression. There is no difference between reducing recoil or having it. And its damage is just long-term safe and pathetic. It feels too safe to use and doesn't take any risks in terms of design unlike other ballistic weapons like Heavy Mortar, Chaingun or MK IX. Thus it has been reverted to its old state with a massive twist. Making it far more unhinged in nature

Devastator now fires 200 HE explosive damage projectiles at 100 flux cost each. Instead of 150 at 75.
With increased flux spending, this weapon will now tax ships like Invictus or Legion more heavily. But with increased damage it will now feel far more potent against targets other than fighters. Encouraging players to use it on something like a Dominator especially with the current state of things.

Hellbore Cannon projectile speed increased by 50%
Hellbore's inability to damage shields and low DPS means that it's really easy to counter. And has been slowly falling out of existence. Quietly ignored in vanilla. With increased projectile speed and Hephaestus design changes. Hellbore is now the safer option... That also suffers from the inability to suppress its target

Assault Chaingun now has 600 range instead of 450.
Chaingun has no place in vanilla on ships other than SO ones. And it has also been ceasing to exist slowly due to the viability of Heavy Blaster against armour replacing it instead. With additional 150 range it is now extremely threatening. Being able to be equipped on something like a Falcon to tear down anything in its wake

Gauss Cannon now does 1000 damage instead of 700 per shot.
This has been done because Gauss Cannon is generally considered now the weakest weapon in the game. And it requires heavy buffs to make itself viable

Mjolnir now does 400 EMP damage instead of 200 per shot.
I was looking to buff the Mjolnir without making it overpowered. And then realised one of its most important aspects is actually irrelevant in vanilla due to how weak the actual stat is

Missile Changes

Missiles have been greatly increased in damage to make them interact with PD better and punish ships without PD significantly harder. Giving proper reasoning to buffing ships like Hyperion. Shrike. And buffing PD tools like interceptors or base PD like Vulcan. In vanilla PD is usually frowned upon to the extreme. Rendering tools like Guardian PD never seen. And constantly begged to be buffed. Especially evident with the recent Anubis blog post. I have come to a realisation that in order for PD to be actually respected. The threat they are to deal with has to be far more severe.

Harpoon now does 1000 damage instead of 750
Atropos now does 1250 damage instead of 1000
Hammer now does 2000 damage instead of 1500
Sabot now does 250x6 damage instead of 200x5

Breach now does 300 HE damage on top of their passive damage package instead of 150 HE. This will confuse the AI a lot of less

Pilum now does 500 ENERGY damage instead of FRAG. Increased base ammo capacity by a factor of 2

Reaper now does 5k damage instead of 4k. Additionally damage has been changed to Energy instead of HE to encourage shooting shields with it. And also to make it more akin to an actual nuclear warhead than an anti-shield projectile. Reaper launchers have been standardised to compensate. Cyclone no longer provides additional launch speed. And they now provide as many missiles as they have OP. 1 per 2. Cyclone now gives 13. Typhoon now gives 5

Dragonfire Torpedo launchers now have twice as much ammo. Dragon however has less 100 targeting range

Gorgon reworked. Now has 2, 2, 5 missiles [BASE, POD, HYDRA]. Each projectile fires for 5 seconds instead of 1.25. Ending up dealing 3200 damage for Gorgon over the duration of 5 seconds. And 2000 times 6 for Hydra. The damage is now also HE instead of ENERGY

Gazer now has 800 range, but the beam does twice as much damage. Gazer pushing mechanic removed

Squall now does 200 energy damage instead of 100 kinetic for every projectile. Turning stats increased to make it miss the target less

Hurricane now deploys 15 projectiles instead of 7

Swarmer deploys 8 instead of 4 projectiles per salvo. And has 120 ammo instead of 80. DOES NOT AFFECT TALON VARIANT

Locust now launchers projectiles 50% faster and has 33% more ammo capacity

Annihilator rockets are now launched at 100 instead of 50 units. And accelerate to 500 speed instead of 400. Additionally they have 50% more ammo. Base Annihilator now has 80 ammo instead of 50. POD now has 150. And fighter Annihilator now has 8 instead of 4

Salamander now does 500 HE damage

END OF MISSILE CHANGES

Beams have been thoroughly overhauled in damage capabilities and general impact so that they are less spammy. More difficult to utilise. Whilst at the same time ridiculously impactful in combat

Phase Lance has 800 range but 1 flux efficiency

Graviton Beam, Tactical Laser, HIL, IR Autolance range is now 800 but DPS is now twice as high at same flux efficiency. Meaning HIL now does 1k HE damage per second at 800 flux cost for example.

Graviton pushing mechanic removed. As it was too frustrating to deal with and had no counter of any kind

Tachyon Lance, Ion Beam do twice as much EMP damage instead, but do not gain flux costs

PD WEAPON CHANGES

HMG now does twice as much damage per projectile. Topping at whopping 640 kinetic DPS.
Now has 400 range instead of 450
LMG, DLMG range increased to 400
Both HMG and LMG were PD weapons that failed at their job. And only existed in fringe melee SO builds. They are now more effective at both melee builds and PD role. Being far less fatal to ships when the autofit decides to equip them. They are however still less effective at PD than Vulcan than Flak Cannon. But with this alternative role it's not as big of a deal

Vulcan range increased to 500. This does affect Talons
Dual Flak Cannon now has 500 range and does 200 fragmentation damage per projectile at 0.66 firing cooldown. Meaning it does 33% more damage than Flak Cannon and has the same range. As previously Flak Cannon had 500 range and Dual Flak Cannon had 400
These weapons funnily enough did their job well enough. But with the incredible spread, Vulcan could have 500 range without it feeling too bad to fight against.
Comically, this change hasn't been motivated by LMG necessarily being stronger. It was motivated by a thought that Mora carriers should be able to use Vulcans without ITU

Paladin PD System now shoots a burst that lasts 0.4 seconds instead of 0.1. Meaning it will deal less fragmentation damage and more energy damage at slower charge spending. This does mean it has higher long-term DPS than Autopulse
Mining Laser, LR PD Laser, PD Laser damage doubled. Flux efficiency remains the same
Burst PD now fires a beam for 0.6 seconds instead of 0.3 (idea taken from a forum post). High Delay Burst PD used by Sparks now uses the same damage values
With these changes PD Lasers will now finally be worth equipping. And goodly so. Cause Front-Shield Conversion is no longer as strong

END OF PD WEAPON CHANGES

ENERGY WEAPON CHANGES

Ion Cannon now does 50 instead of 40 damage at 0.6 flux efficiency. It now additionally has 600 range. Claws are now equipped with the standard Ion Cannon variant. Meaning each of them does 100 DPS
Ion Pulser also has 600 range now

Pulse Laser now fires at efficiency 1 and with 4 shots per second. Ending up at 400 DPS
